title: 3rd Truth 1st Mystery No Degrees In Essential Power

questions.question: What is the main idea of the First Mystery?
questions.answer: Allah’s power is essential to His Being, so weakness cannot touch it, and nothing is hard for Him to create.

questions.question: Why does the passage say the opposite of something essential cannot enter it?
questions.answer: Because that would mean two opposites existing together in the same reality, which is impossible.

questions.question: What opposite of power is discussed, and what is said about it?
questions.answer: Weakness is the opposite, and it can never reach Allah’s Essence.

questions.question: How does the passage explain differences in levels, like stronger and weaker forms of something?
questions.answer: It says such levels appear when an opposite mixes in, like darkness with light or cold with heat.

questions.question: According to the passage, why are there no levels or degrees in Divine power?
questions.answer: Because no opposite, weakness, or deficiency can enter it.

questions.question: What result follows from there being no weakness in Divine power?
questions.answer: Nothing can block it, and creating anything does not become difficult for Allah.

questions.question: What comparison is made between resurrection, spring, a tree, and a flower?
questions.answer: They are all equally easy for Allah to create.

questions.question: Besides ease, what does the passage say about the quality of Allah’s creation of these things?
questions.answer: Each is made with complete artistry, wonder, and wisdom, whether small or great.

questions.question: What would happen, according to the passage, if Divine unity were denied?
questions.answer: Creation would become extremely difficult, and things would lose much of their beauty and value.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the production of living things if Divine unity were not true?
questions.answer: Even a small living thing might take a very long time to be produced, or perhaps not be produced at all.

questions.question: What two qualities of fruits, flowers, trees, and animals are highlighted near the end?
questions.answer: They are very valuable and highly crafted, even though they are many and are made quickly and easily.

questions.question: What do these created things do after they appear in the world?
questions.answer: They show Allah’s glory, carry out their roles, then leave behind seeds and pass on.

questions.question: What claim does the First Mystery make about Allah’s power and His Essence?
questions.answer: It teaches that Allah’s power belongs essentially to His Essence and is not something separate or borrowed.

questions.question: Why is it impossible for weakness to affect Divine power?
questions.answer: Because weakness is the opposite of power, and opposites cannot enter an essential reality of this kind.

questions.question: What examples are given to show how different levels happen in created things?
questions.answer: The passage points to light and darkness, heat and cold, and strength and resistance.

questions.question: What do these examples help the reader understand about Divine power?
questions.answer: They show that created things have varying levels because opposites affect them, but Divine power has no such mixture.

questions.question: If Divine power has no degrees, what does that mean for creation?
questions.answer: It means Allah creates all things without strain, and no task is harder than another for Him.

questions.question: How does the passage use the examples of spring, a tree, and a flower?
questions.answer: It uses them to show that very large and very small acts of creation are equally easy for Allah.

questions.question: What does the passage say about resurrection in relation to other created things?
questions.answer: It says resurrection is no harder for Allah than bringing spring, a tree, or a flower into existence.

questions.question: What idea about artistic beauty is connected to these acts of creation?
questions.answer: Ease does not reduce quality; Allah creates each thing with beauty, wisdom, and perfection.

questions.question: What role does Divine unity play in making creation understandable in the passage?
questions.answer: Divine unity explains how many valuable and complex things can be created easily, quickly, and in order.

questions.question: What problem would appear if that unity were absent?
questions.answer: Small things could become harder to make than large ones, and the process of creation would become confused and burdensome.

questions.question: What inference can a reader make from the phrase that living things appear regularly on the plain of being?
questions.answer: Their coming into existence is not random; it happens in an ordered and repeated way under Allah’s power.

questions.question: What remains after these living things complete their duties, and why is that important?
questions.answer: Their seeds remain, showing continuity, order, and the wise passing on of life.

questions.question: What principle does the passage begin with about something that is essential?
questions.answer: If a quality truly belongs to a thing’s essence, its opposite cannot be part of that essence.

questions.question: How is that principle applied to Allah’s power?
questions.answer: Since power is essential to Allah, powerlessness can never be part of Him.

questions.question: What logical problem would happen if both power and powerlessness were joined in the same essence?
questions.answer: It would be an impossible joining of opposites.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the reason created things can have stronger and weaker forms?
questions.answer: Their levels come from the presence or influence of opposing factors.

questions.question: Why is Allah’s power not described as stronger in one case and weaker in another?
questions.answer: Because nothing opposite to it can enter it, so it does not vary or decline.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about obstacles in relation to Divine power?
questions.answer: Obstacles cannot stop it or make any act of creation harder.

questions.question: How does the passage challenge the idea that resurrection is too great to believe?
questions.answer: It says resurrection is just as easy for Allah as bringing forth spring.

questions.question: What comparison shows that size does not matter to Divine power?
questions.answer: A flower, a tree, a spring, and the final resurrection are all equally manageable for Allah.

questions.question: What does the passage say would happen to the art and worth of creation without Divine unity?
questions.answer: They would be reduced, and creation would no longer appear with the same beauty and value.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the present reality of the natural world as evidence?
questions.answer: Precious and beautifully made living things appear everywhere in abundance, speed, and order before our eyes.

questions.question: What duties do fruits, flowers, trees, and animals perform according to the passage?
questions.answer: They serve their created purposes while glorifying Allah.

questions.question: What does their leaving seeds behind suggest about Allah’s creation?
questions.answer: It shows wise planning, continuity, and the smooth renewal of life.

questions.question: According to the First Mystery, what makes Divine power different from created forms of power?
questions.answer: Divine power is essential, complete, and untouched by weakness or limitation.

questions.question: What basic rule about opposites is used to support that point?
questions.answer: An essential reality cannot contain its direct opposite.

questions.question: Which illustrations are used to explain how levels appear in created things?
questions.answer: The passage mentions light mixed with darkness, heat mixed with cold, and strength challenged by resistance.

questions.question: Why are these examples important for understanding the argument?
questions.answer: They show that variation comes from outside interference, which Divine power does not have.

questions.question: What conclusion does the passage draw from the absence of degrees in Divine power?
questions.answer: Allah creates everything as easily as if He were creating only one thing.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about difficulty in relation to Allah’s acts?
questions.answer: No created thing is hard for Him, and no barrier can stand against His power.

questions.question: How does the passage connect this teaching to the resurrection?
questions.answer: It presents resurrection as no more difficult than the yearly renewal of spring.

questions.question: In what way does the passage compare a tree and a flower?
questions.answer: It says creating the one is no harder than creating the other.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the quality of Allah’s work in both small and great things?
questions.answer: Both are made with equal beauty, wisdom, and extraordinary design.

questions.question: What would the world be like if Divine unity were not the truth, according to the passage?
questions.answer: Creation would become difficult, delayed, and stripped of much of its fine artistry.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the appearance of living things in this world now?
questions.answer: They come into existence in an orderly and repeated way, despite being many, precious, and detailed.

questions.question: What final picture does the passage give of the life cycle of these beings?
questions.answer: They enter the world, fulfill their roles in praise of Allah, and leave seeds to continue what comes after them.

questions.question: What is the first lesson taught in this passage about Allah’s power?
questions.answer: Allah’s power is inseparable from His Essence, so weakness can never belong to Him.

questions.question: How does the passage support this lesson through reasoning?
questions.answer: It argues that an essence cannot admit its opposite without becoming contradictory and impossible.

questions.question: What pattern in the created world is used to explain the idea of degrees?
questions.answer: Things show higher and lower levels when opposing qualities affect them.

questions.question: Give one example from the passage of such opposing qualities.
questions.answer: One example is brightness becoming stronger or weaker depending on darkness.

questions.question: Why does the passage deny that such degrees apply to Divine power?
questions.answer: Because Divine power has no opposing force mixed into it.

questions.question: What does this mean about Allah’s ability to create many different things?
questions.answer: He creates all of them without hardship, whether they are small, large, few, or many.

questions.question: What comparison does the passage make to help the reader understand this?
questions.answer: It compares the final resurrection, springtime, a tree, and a flower as equally easy for Allah.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest about the artistic excellence of creation?
questions.answer: Ease does not reduce excellence; every level of creation is made with remarkable skill.

questions.question: How does the passage use a contrast involving Divine unity?
questions.answer: It says that without Divine unity, creation would become far more difficult and less beautiful.

questions.question: What does the statement about an animate being taking a year or never appearing at all emphasize?
questions.answer: It stresses how impossible and disordered creation would be without the truth of Divine unity.

questions.question: Why is the abundance of fruits, flowers, trees, and animals important in the argument?
questions.answer: Their abundance, along with their value and beauty, shows that they are created by limitless power.

questions.question: What happens after these beings finish their time in the world?
questions.answer: They leave seeds behind and depart after completing the purpose given to them.

questions.question: What central truth does the First Mystery try to make clear?
questions.answer: Allah’s power has no weakness, no levels of deficiency, and no difficulty in creating anything.

questions.question: Why can the opposite of an essential attribute not enter the essence it belongs to?
questions.answer: Because that would destroy the meaning of the attribute by combining opposites in an impossible way.

questions.question: How is this truth specifically linked to Allah?
questions.answer: Since power belongs essentially to Allah, helplessness can never approach Him.

questions.question: What is the relationship between degrees and opposites in the passage?
questions.answer: Degrees appear when an opposite is present and affects the thing.

questions.question: What examples help explain this relationship?
questions.answer: The passage uses the examples of light with darkness, heat with cold, and strength with resistance.

questions.question: What follows from saying that Divine power has no degrees?
questions.answer: It follows that no obstacle can hinder it and no act of creation can weigh it down.

questions.question: How does the passage answer someone who thinks resurrection is too hard to imagine?
questions.answer: It says Allah brings about resurrection as easily as He brings a flower or spring into existence.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the way Allah creates a flower, a tree, spring, and resurrection?
questions.answer: He creates each with the same ease and with fitting beauty and wonder.

questions.question: What teaching from the Risale-i Nur is mentioned about denying Divine unity?
questions.answer: It states that without Divine unity, even simple acts of creation would become harder than greater ones and lose their excellence.

questions.question: What can students infer from the phrase that these beings appear on the plain of being?
questions.answer: Their existence is brought out into the world in an organized and visible way by Allah’s command.

questions.question: Which features of living things are paired together in the final paragraph?
questions.answer: Their great value is paired with their abundance, and their fine artistry is paired with their quick and easy creation.

questions.question: How does the passage end the description of these beings’ role in creation?
questions.answer: It ends by showing them praising Allah through their state, doing their assigned work, and leaving seeds behind before passing on.
